evidence: src/application/require-order.ts: requireOrder is the only place that throws DomainError("not_found"). advance-order-use-case.ts, cancel-order-use-case.ts and get-order-use-case.ts all call it.
src/application/order-dto.ts: toOrderDto is used by every order-returning use case (advance, cancel, get, list-by-state, place).

src/application/place-order-use-case.ts and src/application/cancel-order-use-case.ts call the domain functions reserveStock and releaseStock, so the stock rule is not duplicated in the application layer.
src/application/list-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps products to StockLevelDto inline. This is a minor inconsistency with toOrderDto, not a bypass.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All eight files are application-layer use cases and their shared helpers. They serve one concern: orchestrating order lifecycle and stock queries through domain repositories. Each use case has a single execute entry point and takes repository abstractions through the constructor. Shared rules live in one place each. The "order not found" rule is only in requireOrder, and Advance, Cancel and Get all use it. Order-to-DTO mapping is only in toOrderDto. Stock reservation and release are delegated to the domain functions reserveStock and releaseStock, not reimplemented in Place and Cancel. Two small blemishes don't amount to a split or a bypass. StockLevelDto sits in order-dto.ts, and ListStockLevelsUseCase maps to it inline instead of through a mapper. The product save loop also appears in both Place and Cancel.
